title: Derived mapping spaces of left proper cell colimits
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the complete, cocomplete model-category conventions and homotopy function complexes of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a left proper combinatorial model category with functorial factorizations; left proper means that a pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence, and combinatorial has the meaning of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Homotopy colimits and their comparison maps mean colimits of projectively cofibrant replacements as in [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. The following two comparisons hold with no cofibrancy assumption on the displayed objects.

(a) For a span $B\leftarrow A\to X$ with $A\to B$ a cofibration, its ordinary pushout $P=B\amalg_A X$ is a homotopy pushout: the comparison from its model homotopy colimit to $P$ is a weak equivalence. Consequently, for every originally fibrant $Z$, the canonical comparison is an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(P,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\mathbin{\times^h}_{\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)}\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z).$$
Here $\times^h$ is the limit of the displayed diagram in the infinity category of spaces.

(b) Let $\theta$ be a small nonzero limit ordinal and let $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ be a diagram of cofibrations, continuous at every nonzero limit ordinal $\beta<\theta$, meaning $X_\beta=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ with its given cocone. Its ordinary colimit is a homotopy colimit, and for every originally fibrant $Z$ the comparison is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\theta}X_\alpha,Z)\simeq\operatorname{lim}_{\alpha<\theta}^{h}\operatorname{Map}^h(X_\alpha,Z),$$
where the limit is indexed by the opposite ordinal and retains the restriction maps. No simplicial enrichment is assumed.

proof.text: Fix a small ordinary category $I$ and write $\mathcal A=\mathcal M^I$ with the projective model structure of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], and $F=\operatorname{colim}_I$. Its weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], $F$ is left adjoint to the constant-diagram functor, so a lifting square for $Ff$ against a (trivial) fibration is the same as a square for $f$ against its constant diagram. Consequently $F$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. It also preserves ordinary pushouts: a map out of either the colimit of a pointwise pushout or the pushout of the colimits is exactly a compatible pair of cocones agreeing on the common diagram.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.7, printed p. 44; agent expansion of its homotopy-colimit inputs

proof.text: Every projective cofibration is objectwise a cofibration. Indeed evaluation at $i$ has right adjoint $R_i(Y)(j)=\prod_{a:j\to i}Y$, with transition maps reindexing factors. This adjunction follows by taking the component indexed by $1_i$ in one direction and composing with diagram structure maps in the other. Products of trivial fibrations have the right lifting property against every cofibration: solve the square separately in each factor. Hence $R_i$ sends trivial fibrations to objectwise trivial fibrations. The adjoint lifting square for a projective cofibration $f$ shows that $f_i$ has the left lifting property against every trivial fibration, and is a cofibration. Pushouts in $\mathcal A$ are pointwise by their cocone universal property; left properness of $\mathcal M$ now implies left properness of $\mathcal A$. In both categories the closure of cofibrations under composition and pushout is [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure].

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.7, printed p. 44; agent expansion of its homotopy-colimit inputs

proof.text: Here is the relative factorization calculation needed to allow a noncofibrant base. Suppose $K\to U$ and $K\to V$ are cofibrations in $\mathcal A$ and $w:U\to V$ is a weak equivalence under $K$. Form $U\amalg_K V$ and factor its map $(w,1):U\amalg_K V\to V$ as a cofibration $j$ followed by a trivial fibration $p:T\to V$. Both coprojections into the pushout are cofibrations by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], so their composites $i:U\to T$ and $s:V\to T$ with $j$ are cofibrations. The identities $pi=w$ and $ps=1_V$ make $i$ and $s$ weak equivalences by two-out-of-three. Step 1 makes $F(i)$ and $F(s)$ weak equivalences. From $F(p)F(s)=1$ and then $F(w)=F(p)F(i)$, two-out-of-three gives that $F(w)$ is a weak equivalence. This calculation assumes only cofibrancy relative to $K$, not cofibrancy of $K,U,V$.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12, printed pp. 6-7, relative split-factorization argument expanded directly in the projective model

proof.text: Suppose $K\to D$ is a projective cofibration, $K'$ is projectively cofibrant, $v:K'\to K$ is an objectwise weak equivalence, and $F(v)$ is a weak equivalence. Factor $K'\to K\to D$ as a projective cofibration $K'\to E$ followed by an objectwise trivial fibration $e:E\to D$. Put $T=E\amalg_{K'}K$. By Step 2, $E\to T$ is an objectwise weak equivalence, so the induced $t:T\to D$ is one by $e=t\circ(E\to T)$ and two-out-of-three. Both $K\to T$ and $K\to D$ are projective cofibrations, so Step 3 gives that $F(t)$ is a weak equivalence. On the other hand $F(E)\to F(T)=F(E)\amalg_{F(K')}F(K)$ is the pushout of the weak equivalence $F(v)$ along the cofibration $F(K')\to F(E)$; left properness of $\mathcal M$ makes it a weak equivalence. Thus $F(e):F(E)\to F(D)$ is a weak equivalence. The diagram $E$ is projectively cofibrant, since $K'$ is, so $e$ is a projectively cofibrant replacement of $D$. For any other projectively cofibrant replacement $q:QD\to D$, lift $q$ against the objectwise trivial fibration $e:E\to D$, using cofibrancy of $QD$. The resulting $l:QD\to E$ satisfies $el=q$ and is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Applying Step 3 with initial base shows that $F(l)$ is a weak equivalence. Therefore $F(q)=F(e)F(l)$, the canonical comparison $F(QD)\to F(D)$, is a weak equivalence as well. This last comparison only requires that $q$ be a weak equivalence with projectively cofibrant source.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.7, printed p. 44; agent expansion of its homotopy-colimit inputs

proof.text: For (a), let $I$ be the three-object span category and $D=(B\leftarrow A\to X)$. Let $K=(A\xleftarrow{1}A\to X)$ with map to $D$ equal to the identity at $A,X$ and to the given cofibration $A\to B$ at $B$. This is a projective cofibration: in a square against an objectwise trivial fibration, the lifts at $A,X$ are already prescribed by the map from $K$, and the lift at $B$ is obtained from the single lifting square with left side $A\to B$. Choose a cofibrant replacement $QA\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and factor $QA\to A\to X$ as a cofibration $QA\to\widetilde X$ followed by a trivial fibration $\widetilde X\xrightarrow{\sim}X$. Set $K'=(QA\xleftarrow{1}QA\to\widetilde X)$. It is projectively cofibrant: first lift $QA$ against the objectwise trivial fibration at the middle vertex, set the lift at the repeated $QA$ using the structure map, and extend the lift to $\widetilde X$ along $QA\to\widetilde X$. The componentwise maps give an objectwise weak equivalence $K'\to K$. Their colimits are $\widetilde X\to X$, a weak equivalence: a cocone on either span is uniquely determined by its component at its right vertex because the other arrow is the identity. All hypotheses of Step 4 hold. Therefore the canonical comparison $\operatorname{hocolim}_I D\to B\amalg_A X$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.7, printed p. 44; agent expansion of its homotopy-colimit inputs

proof.text: For (b), regard the small ordinal $\theta$ as a category and let $D_\alpha=X_\alpha$. Put $K=\operatorname{const}X_0$ with the cocone maps to $D$. We verify that $K\to D$ is a projective cofibration by giving its lifting property against an arbitrary objectwise trivial fibration $p:U\to V$. In such a square, the map $K\to U$ prescribes the lift at $0$. Given compatible lifts $h_\gamma:X_\gamma\to U_\gamma$ through stage $\alpha$, compose $h_\alpha$ with $U_\alpha\to U_{\alpha+1}$ and lift against $p_{\alpha+1}$ using the cofibration $X_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$. The resulting $h_{\alpha+1}$ has the required restrictions to every earlier stage by composition. At a nonzero limit $\beta<\theta$, the maps $X_\gamma\xrightarrow{h_\gamma}U_\gamma\to U_\beta$ for $\gamma<\beta$ form a cocone. Continuity of $D$ and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] give a unique $h_\beta:X_\beta\to U_\beta$. Its equation with $p_\beta$ and its equation on $X_0$ follow by checking all colimit coprojections. Thus transfinite recursion yields a natural lift on all of $\theta$. This proves projective cofibrancy relative to $K$ directly and makes no assertion about preservation of weak equivalences by arbitrary limit-stage colimits.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.7, printed p. 44; agent expansion of its homotopy-colimit inputs

proof.text: Choose a cofibrant replacement $QX_0\xrightarrow{\sim}X_0$ and put $K'=\operatorname{const}QX_0$. This diagram is projectively cofibrant: in a lifting square against an objectwise trivial fibration, choose its component at $0$ using cofibrancy of $QX_0$ and then define each other component by the unique structure arrow $0\to\alpha$. The natural map $K'\to K$ is objectwise a weak equivalence. Its colimit is the same weak equivalence $QX_0\to X_0$, since a cocone on a constant diagram indexed by an ordinal with initial object $0$ is a single map: compatibility along $0\to\alpha$ forces every component to equal the component at $0$. The nonzero hypothesis supplies that vertex. Applying Step 4 with Step 6 proves that $\operatorname{hocolim}_{\alpha<\theta}X_\alpha\to\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\theta}X_\alpha$ is a weak equivalence. The construction works for all small ordinal cofinalities and only uses the stated continuity.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.7, printed p. 44; agent expansion of its homotopy-colimit inputs

proof.text: For either the span of Step 5 or the ordinal diagram of Step 7, [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] says that the localized ordinary cocone of a projectively cofibrant replacement is a colimit cocone. Write $r:QD\to D$ for the replacement, $\iota_i^Q:QD_i\to F(QD)$ and $\iota_i:D_i\to F(D)$ for the colimit maps, and $c=F(r)$. For every $i$, the defining colimit equation is $c\iota_i^Q=\iota_i r_i$, and these equations are compatible with every arrow of $I$ because $r$ is a natural transformation. Applying $q$ gives an equivalence between these entire cocones: each $q(r_i)$ and the apex map $q(c)$ are equivalences by the comparisons just proved. Thus the original localized cocone, including its specified legs, is colimiting. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], mapping this cocone into $qZ$ gives the limit of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qD_i,qZ)$ over $I^{\mathrm{op}}$, including its actual restriction maps. By [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], these localization mapping spaces are exactly $\operatorname{Map}^h(D_i,Z)$ and the corresponding mapping space from the colimit is $\operatorname{Map}^h(\operatorname{colim}_I D,Z)$, naturally in the homotopy theory of the inputs; the original objects may first be replaced by cofibrant objects as that node permits. When $I$ is the span, its opposite limit is the homotopy pullback displayed in (a). When $I=\theta$, it is the homotopy limit over the opposite ordinal displayed in (b). The given fibrancy of $Z$ suffices for the function-complex representatives. No simplicial enrichment or cofibrancy of any original object has been introduced.
